text: [See Loyola Marymount Univ. v. Hartford Acc. & Indem. Co., supra, 219 CA3d at 1222, 271 CR at 531; and Frank & Freedus v. Allstate Ins. Co. (1996) 45 CA4th 461, 470, 52 CR2d 678, 683] The ISO endorsement also states that the exclusion applies “whether the insured may be liable as an employer or in any other capacity.” Absent this language, an employment-related practices exclusion does not preclude coverage for claims against the insured by employees of an independent contractor. [North American Bldg. Maint., Inc. v. Fireman's Fund Ins. Co., supra, 137 CA4th at 638, 40 CR3d at 476—subcontractor's employees performing work on insured's premises sued insured for labor violations and false imprisonment] (a) Interpretation 1) [3:381] “Employment-related”: The term “employment-related” is not ambiguous; it is “used in its ordinary sense, i.e., related to employment,” and “modifies the specified acts” (discipline, demotion, etc.).
